parts.text:
36 A student has a set of identical cells and identical lamps. The cells have negligible internal
resistance.
A lamp connected to a cell lights with normal brightness.
What happens when the student connects the lamps and the cells as shown?
2
1
3
A
All three lamps light with normal brightness.
B
Only lamp 2 lights with normal brightness.
C
Only lamps 1 and 3 light with normal brightness.
D
None of the lamps light with normal brightness.

hints: Notice that lamp 1 is in series with the left cell and lamp 3 is in series with the right cell, while lamp 2 is connected vertically between the two middle junction dots.
Compare the potential at the top and bottom of lamp 2: by symmetry each side is one cell terminal away from the bottom wire, so the two ends of lamp 2 are at the same potential.
Recall normal brightness means the lamp has the same p.d. as one lamp across one cell, so check which lamps still have that full cell p.d. across them.
walkthrough: Define normal brightness from the first diagram: one identical lamp across one cell of e.m.f. $E$ has p.d. $V = E$ and power $P = V^2/R$.
In the second circuit, trace the left loop and right loop. The top and bottom dots are common junctions, and lamp 2 is connected directly between them.

By symmetry the left side and right side are identical: lamp 1 with the left cell and lamp 3 with the right cell give the same voltage drops, so the top dot and bottom dot define the same p.d. for both sides.
This means the p.d. across the vertical lamp 2 is $V_2 = 0$, so its current and power are zero and it does not light.
Lamps 1 and 3 each still have the full $E$ across them because negligible internal resistance means the cell terminal p.d. stays at $E$, so $P = E^2/R$ as in the first circuit.
Therefore lamps 1 and 3 light with normal brightness and lamp 2 does not. This is option C.

A.explanation: Lamp 2 does not have one cell p.d. across it, so it cannot be at normal brightness with lamps 1 and 3.

B.explanation: Lamp 2 has the same potential at its top and bottom terminals by symmetry, so $V=0$ across it and it does not light normally.

C.explanation: Lamps 1 and 3 each have a full cell p.d. across them while lamp 2 has zero p.d., so only lamps 1 and 3 are at normal brightness.

D.explanation: Lamps 1 and 3 are each in a separate loop with one cell, so they still receive normal voltage and power.
